title: The bishop sacrifice on h7 (Greek gift)

D0.outcome: States the conditions for the sacrifice on h7 (the knight can reach g5, the queen can reach h5, the bishop is on the diagonal, no defending knight or bishop covers) and what the sacrifice is for.

D1.outcome: When told 'Greek gift', finds Bxh7+ and the follow-up, and names the conditions that hold.

D2.outcome: In a mixed set, plays it only where the conditions hold, declines where a defender covers h7 or h5 or the king escapes, and recognises the declined line.

D3.outcome: Calculates the declined lines and predicts which single defender (knight on f6, a covering bishop) kills it.

misconceptions: The sacrifice on h7 always works.
The sacrifice works whenever the bishop is on the diagonal.
sources: sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §4 CI-27, CI-29; §8 item 13 (conditions are ours; verify by engine)
conditions: The sacrifice is supported by two pieces.
Verified at the wins-or-mates level, never as an unqualified correct answer; practical versus sound is labelled.
contrasts: The same sacrifice with a defender piece covering h7 or h5.
The greedy 'famous sacrifice' where the declined line refutes it; every attack family needs such items.
